final.answer: Among the items returned on the path from P-2-1 to E-38-1, only E-38-1 has a maximum allowable (design) pressure in its datasheet: 10.3 barg (150 psig) per ASME code, or 16.0 barg (232 psig) per PED, depending on the pressure vessel code. The other items on the path (BV-19-1, TV-19-2, CHV-19-1, CHV-19-2) have datasheet values only for stem torque or cracking pressure, not maximum allowable pressure, so no lower value exists; E-38-1 at 10.3 barg is therefore the lowest maximum allowable pressure on the path.

MATCH (a:PlantItem {tag:'P-2-1'}), (b:PlantItem {tag:'E-38-1'})
MATCH p = shortestPath((a)-[:line_to*]->(b))
WITH [n IN nodes(p) | n] AS pathItems
UNWIND pathItems AS it
WITH DISTINCT it WHERE it.tag IS NOT NULL
OPTIONAL MATCH (it)-[:DESCRIBED_BY]->(dev)
WITH it, dev WHERE dev IS NOT NULL
MATCH (d) WHERE d.document_id = dev.document_id AND (d:plm__PCA_100029511 OR d:plm__PCA_100029508 OR d:plm__PCA_100029510)
WITH it, d WHERE toLower(coalesce(d.plm__PCA_100029521,'')) CONTAINS 'maximum allowable'
   OR toLower(coalesce(d.plm__PCA_100029521,'')) CONTAINS 'max allowable'
   OR toLower(coalesce(d.plm__PCA_100029521,'')) CONTAINS 'mawp'
   OR toLower(coalesce(d.plm__PCA_100029522,'')) CONTAINS 'maximum allowable'
   OR (toLower(coalesce(d.plm__PCA_100029521,'')) CONTAINS 'design' AND toLower(coalesce(d.plm__PCA_100029521,'')) CONTAINS 'pressure')
OPTIONAL MATCH (d)-[:plm__PCA_100029520]->(cs:plm__PCA_100029524)

final.answer: The flow path from E-7-2 to GV-47-2 passes through E-7-2, LV-7-1, P-26-1, E-26-1, P-26-2, BV-26-1, P-26-3, LV-26-1, E-45-1, PV-45-1, E-45-2, CHV-45-1, E-45-3, BV-45-1, P-45-1, P-47-1, CHV-47-1 and GV-47-2, and every item on the path has a datasheet. The heat exchangers E-7-2, E-26-1, E-45-1, E-45-2 and E-45-3 (Alfa Laval M3, FG frame) are rated 10.3 barg (150 psig) to ASME or 16.0 barg (232 psig) to PED. The pumps P-26-1, P-26-2, P-26-3, P-45-1 and P-47-1 (Gorman-Rupp) are rated 250 psi (1723 kPa) maximum operating pressure, with 266 psi (1834 kPa) maximum casing pressure, valid up to 100 °F (37 °C). The ball valves LV-7-1, BV-26-1, LV-26-1 and BV-45-1 (Flowserve Worcester F51/F52) have no single maximum pressure; per their pressure/temperature chart they range from about 12 bar (Group 1.2 Class 150 at 250 °C) up to about 51.8 bar (Group 1.2 Class 300 at −30 °C), also limited by seat material. The globe valve PV-45-1 (Fisher ET) likewise has no single figure; its limit depends on the ASME class (CL150/300/600), PN rating (PN16–PN100 depending on variant) and packing (up to 1500 psig / 104 bar for graphite ULF packing). The check valves CHV-45-1 and CHV-47-1 (Swagelok) have no single figure either; working pressures range from 13.7 bar (8C) up to 6000 psig (413 bar) for CH4/CH8 at low temperature. The lowest maximum allowable pressure on the path belongs to GV-47-2, the solenoid valve, which is rated a maximum permissible pressure of only 6 bar gauge (working range 0.5–6 bar), and even that holds only up to 40 °C, with the permissible pressure falling between 40 and 50 °C and a hard stop at 50 °C. So GV-47-2 at 6 bar is the weakest item on the path.

final.answer: Three items receive flow directly from P-5-2: ball valve BV-5-2, globe valve GV-5-1 and centrifugal pump P-12-1. Per its datasheet, GV-5-1 (solenoid valve) has a maximum permissible pressure of 6 bar gauge (PN 6, valid up to 40 °C, with reduced ratings between 40 and 50 °C). P-12-1 (pump) has a maximum operating pressure of 250 psi (1723 kPa, about 17 bar) up to 100 °F, with a maximum casing pressure of 266 psi. For BV-5-2 the datasheet gives no single rated pressure; its allowable pressure depends on pressure class, body material group and seat material per the ASME B16.34 chart (e.g. about 19–20 bar at low temperature for Class 150 options, higher for Class 300), so no specific value can be stated for that valve. Of the three, GV-5-1 has the lowest maximum allowable pressure at 6 bar.

MATCH (p:PlantItem {tag:'P-5-2'})-[:line_to]->(d:PlantItem)
WITH DISTINCT d
OPTIONAL MATCH (d)-[:DESCRIBED_BY]->(dev)
OPTIONAL MATCH (dt)
WHERE dt.document_id = dev.document_id
  AND (dt:plm__PCA_100029511 OR dt:plm__PCA_100029508 OR dt:plm__PCA_100029510)
  AND (toLower(coalesce(dt.plm__PCA_100029521,'')) CONTAINS 'temperature'
       OR toLower(coalesce(dt.plm__PCA_100029521,'')) CONTAINS 'media temp'
       OR toLower(coalesce(dt.plm__PCA_100029521,'')) CONTAINS 'fluid temp'
       OR toLower(coalesce(dt.plm__PCA_100029521,'')) CONTAINS 'operating temp'
       OR toLower(coalesce(dt.plm__PCA_100029522,'')) CONTAINS '°c')
OPTIONAL MATCH (dt)-[:plm__PCA_100029514]->(fn)
OPTIONAL MATCH (dt)-[:plm__PCA_100029520]->(cs)
OPTIONAL MATCH (dt)-[:plm__PCA_100029525]->(src)
WITH d, max(dt.lis__datumValue) AS maxTemp,
     collect(DISTINCT dt.plm__PCA_100029521 + ' = ' + coalesce(dt.plm__PCA_100029522,'') +
             (CASE WHEN cs IS NOT NULL THEN ' [' + cs.rdfs__label + ']' ELSE '' END)) AS values,
     collect(DISTINCT fn.plm__PCA_100029522) AS footnotes,
     collect(DISTINCT src.plm__PCA_100029521) AS sources
WITH collect({tag: d.tag, t: maxTemp, vals: values, fns: footnotes, srcs: sources}) AS items
UNWIND items AS e
WITH e, min([x IN items | x.t]) AS lowest
RETURN e.tag AS tag, e.t AS max_fluid_temperature, e.vals AS matching_values,
       e.fns AS footnotes, e.srcs AS source_sections, lowest AS lowest_max_temperature,
       (e.t = lowest) AS is_lowest, (e.t IS NULL) AS no_datasheet_temperature
ORDER BY e.t ASC, e.tag
LIMIT 80

final.answer: P-26-2 directly feeds two items: ball valve BV-26-1 and check valve CHV-26-1. For BV-26-1 (Flowserve Worcester F51/F52 ball valve), the datasheet gives no single maximum pressure — it depends on the pressure/temperature rating chart (ASME B16.34): for example Class 150 Group 1.2 is about 19.4 bar at 50 °C, Class 300 Group 1.2 up to about 51.8 bar at low temperature, and the seat material can limit it further (e.g. Virgin PTFE 47.0 bar at 100 °C, Delrin 51.7 bar, PEEK 32.8 bar at 250 °C). For CHV-26-1 (Swagelok check valve family), the rating also depends on the variant: up to 6000 psig (413 bar) for the CH series in 316 SS, 3000 psig (206 bar) for the C/CA/CP/CPA series, and 2000 psig (137 bar) in 316 SS or 1500 psig (103 bar) in brass for the 12C/16C sizes. Even the lowest rating in the check-valve family (about 103 bar) is well above the highest possible rating of the ball valve (about 51.8 bar), so BV-26-1 has the lowest maximum allowable pressure of the two.

E-21-1 has the lowest maximum allowable pressure: its datasheet gives 10.3 barg (150 psig) if built to the ASME code, or 16.0 barg (232 psig) if built to the PED code. Along the path: E-7-2, E-26-1, E-45-1, E-45-2 and E-45-3 each have a maximum design pressure of 16.0 barg under PED or 10.3 barg under ASME; LV-7-1, BV-26-1, LV-26-1 and BV-45-1 have no single value stated, as it depends on configuration and temperature; P-26-1, P-26-2, P-26-3, P-45-1 and P-47-1 have a maximum operating pressure of 250 psi (and maximum casing pressure of 266 psi); PV-45-1 has no general valve maximum stated (104 bar is listed for a specific packing system); CHV-45-1 and CHV-47-1 have a stated series maximum working pressure of 6000 psig (413 bar). Tool result:
Datasheet gorman-rupp-0700286, pages [1, 3, 2]:
The maximum allowable operating pressure is 250 psi (1723 kPa), valid for liquid temperatures up to 100 °F (37 °C) [p. 1].

Details:
- Maximum Operating Pressure: 250 psi (1723 kPa), at temperature = 100 °F (37 °C). This limit is based on system component limitations, not just the pump itself [p. 1].
- Maximum Casing Pressure (the pressure the pump casing itself can take): 266 psi (1834 kPa) [p. 1].
- The performance curves (VGH2 1/2C-B-1 on page 2 and VGH2 1/2C-B-2 on page 3) also state a MAX OPERATING PRESSURE of 250 psi, with the note "SPECIFY PLUMBING ACCORDINGLY" — so your piping must be rated for this pressure too.
- Footnote on page 1: for applications exceeding the maximum pressure and/or temperature, consult the factory.

If you need the maximum pressure for a liquid hotter than 100 °F (37 °C), that is not given in these facts — you would need to consult the factory.
{"tool": "datasheet", "tag": "TV-2-1", "question": "What is the maximum allowable pressure?"}

Tool result:
Datasheet fisher-et-d100022x012, pages [4, 3, 5, 32, 18, 26, 19, 22]:
The datasheet does not give one single "maximum allowable pressure" number — it depends on the valve body, its pressure class and the packing used. Here is what it says:

- **Maximum inlet pressures and temperatures** (Table 1. Specifications, p. 3):
  - Steel and stainless steel bodies, flanged: consistent with Class CL150, 300 and 600 per ASME B16.34.
  - Steel and stainless steel bodies, screwed or welding: consistent with flanged CL600 per ASME B16.34.
  - Cast iron bodies, flanged: consistent with CL125B or 250B per ASME B16.1.
  - Overall rule: "As listed below, unless limited by maximum pressure drop or material temperature capabilities" [p. 3].
- **Pressure ratings by product variant** (p. 5, steel raised-face body): PN16, PN25, PN40, PN63 or PN100, depending on whether the valve is ET, ETR or EAT.
- **Packing limits** (Table 2, p. 5): ENVIRO-SEAL Graphite ULF packing is limited to 104 bar / 1500 psig at up to 316 °C / 600 °F; ENVIRO-SEAL PTFE and Duplex packing to 232 °C / 450 °F (no separate pressure figure given for it in these facts).
- **Pressure drops** (maximum difference across the valve): "same as maximum inlet pressure for the specific construction, except where further limited" — see Figure 13 (standard valves), Figure 14 (Cavitrol III cages) on pages 18–19, or Figure 15 for NACE sour-service valves on page 26 [p. 3]. When ordering, the allowed pressure drop must not exceed the lowest value indicated for the combination of materials selected, and the inlet pressure/temperature must always be limited by the applicable ASME pressure/temperature rating [p. 32].
- Some trims have lower pressure-drop caps: e.g. Trims 4 and 29 may be used up to 99 bar / 1440 psi only with clean dry gas (otherwise 21 bar / 300 psi) [p. 18]; the same applies to Trim 85 [p. 26].
- Repeated warning throughout (e.g. notes on Figures 13–15, pp. 18, 19, 26): do not exceed the maximum pressure and temperature for the pressure rating of the body material used, even though the trim shown may have higher capabilities; also do not exceed any applicable code or standard limitation [p. 5].

I could not find in these facts a single absolute maximum pressure figure for the valve as a whole — the datasheet limits it by pressure class (ASME rating / PN rating), body material and packing choice.

Key values:

- **CH4, CH8 (316 SS body):** 6000 psig (413 bar) at 10°F to 100°F (−12 to 37°C), dropping to 4280 psig (294 bar) at 400°F (204°C). Note: pressure ratings may be limited by the end connection — see Dimensions, page 12 [p. 3].
- **CH16 (316 SS body):** 5000 psig (344 bar) at 10°F to 100°F (−12 to 37°C), dropping to 3560 psig (245 bar) at 400°F (204°C). Same end-connection note [p. 3].
- **C (2C, 4C, 6C, 8C), CA, CP, CPA (316 SS body):** 3000 psig (206 bar) at −10°F to 100°F (−23 to 37°C), dropping to 2185 psig (150 bar) at 375°F (190°C) [p. 3].
- **C (2C, 4C, 6C, 8C), CA, CP, CPA (brass body):** 3000 psig (206 bar) at −10°F to 100°F, dropping to 2405 psig (165 bar) at 250°F (121°C); brass has no rating above 250°F [p. 3].
- **12C, 16C (316 SS):** 2000 psig (137 bar) at −10°F to 100°F; (brass): 1500 psig (103 bar) at −10°F to 100°F [p. 3].

These come from the pressure-temperature rating tables on page 3 — use them to find the working pressure for your specific valve, material, and temperature.

Two related limits if they apply to your setup:

- **Maximum back pressure** (pressure on the outlet side, holding the valve closed) is given at 70°F (20°C) in Technical Data table 1 on page 3 — e.g. 413 bar for CH8 (fixed cracking pressure), 344 bar for CH16, 3000 psig (206 bar) for CA, 4CPA, 8CPA, and 8CP, and 13.7 bar for 8C. It may also be limited by the end connection (see Dimensions, page 12) [p. 3].
- **Deflector caps** (accessory for 4C, 8C, CP, CPA) are rated a maximum of 300 psig (20.6 bar) at 100°F (37°C) [p. 14].
- **Sour gas valves (CH series)** are rated 5000 psig (344 bar) at 70°F (20°C) [p. 14].

I could not find in these facts a single overall "maximum allowable pressure" for all valves — it always depends on the series, body material, temperature, and end connection. If you tell me your exact valve ordering number, check the tables on pages 3 and 12.

Datasheet fisher-et-d100022x012, pages [4, 3, 5, 32, 18, 26, 19, 22]:
The datasheet does not give one single maximum pressure number — the allowable pressure depends on which valve variant, body material/pressure class and packing you have. Here is what it gives:

- **Maximum inlet pressure / temperature:** "Consistent with CL150, 300 and 600 per ASME B16.34" for steel and stainless steel flanged bodies; "Consistent with flanged CL600 per ASME B16.34" for screwed or welding connections; "Consistent with CL125B or 250B per ASME B16.1" for cast iron flanged bodies [p. 3]. (ASME classes are standard pressure-rating levels — the actual value depends on temperature and material.)
- **Pressure ratings for the steel raised-face body by variant:** ET = PN16 or PN100, EAT = PN25 or PN40, ETR = PN40 or PN63 (PN16 also listed for ETR) [p. 5].
- **Packing limit (ENVIRO-SEAL Graphite ULF packing):** maximum pressure 1500 psig / 104 bar at up to 316 °C / 600 °F [p. 5]. ENVIRO-SEAL PTFE and Duplex packing is limited to 232 °C / 450 °F (no pressure figure given for it in these facts).
- **General rule:** the maximum inlet pressures and temperatures apply "unless limited by maximum pressure drop or material temperature capabilities" [p. 3]; the maximum pressure drop is the same as the maximum inlet pressure except where Figures 13, 14 or 15 limit it further, and for Whisper Trim III / Whisper NXG Trim cages (levels A1–D3) it is 0.999 ΔP/P1 maximum [p. 3]. Pressure drop limits are shown in Figure 13 (p. 18), Figure 14 (p. 19) and Figure 15 (p. 26), with the note: do not exceed the maximum pressure and temperature for the pressure rating of the body material used, even though the trim shown may have higher capabilities [pp. 18, 19, 26].
- **Ordering:** the inlet pressure and temperature "must always be limited by the applicable ASME pressure/temperature rating", and the maximum allowable pressure drop must not exceed the lowest value indicated for the combination of materials selected [p. 32].

So: check which body/class and packing you have — the pressure limit is the lowest applicable rating (ASME class per p. 3, PN rating per p. 5, packing limit per p. 5), and never exceed the limits in Figures 13–15 or any applicable code. In other words, the maximum inlet pressure comes from the pressure/temperature tables of these ASME flange classes, which the datasheet itself does not print as numbers.
